classic_text:
## Who should you check with before you decide?

I'd get a few answers before you pick a route. Not all of them, and not all at once. But the people below can each settle a question that this guide can only point at. A house full of belongings is hard enough without finding out halfway through that nobody checked who could sign.

- **Real estate attorney:** who has authority to sell, any probate or trust questions, and what has to be disclosed on the Transfer Disclosure Statement.
- **Listing agent:** how the disclosure form is completed for your specific home, if you are thinking about listing.
- **Title company:** liens, title issues and who has to sign.
- **CPA:** the tax consequences of selling.
- **Insurance professional:** what coverage looks like on a vacant or hazardous property.
- **City or county building, health or fire department:** whether any enforcement notice or local rule applies to the property.

If a notice has already been posted or a letter has come, start with the city or county. It is better to know what is open before you choose a path than to hear about it from a buyer.

[note] Confirm legal, tax, title, code and insurance points with the right professional for your situation. This guide explains the questions to ask. It does not replace the answers.

Once you know who can sign, what is owed and what the city or county says, you can compare keeping it, clearing it, listing it and selling directly with real information. Getting clarity early usually creates more options, not fewer.

If a direct sale is one of the routes you want to talk through, the next step is the [packed and hoarded house page](https://www.twinhomebuyer.com/hoarder-houses/). Read it, then decide. There is no rush attached to it.
team_final_text:
## Who should you check with before you decide?

Before you pick a route, check with an attorney, a title company, a CPA, an insurance professional and your city or county. Each can settle a question this guide can only point at. You do not need all of them at once.

- **Real estate attorney:** who has authority to sell, any probate or trust questions, and what has to be disclosed on the Transfer Disclosure Statement.
- **Listing agent:** how the disclosure form is completed for your specific home, if you are thinking about listing.
- **Title company:** liens, title issues and who has to sign.
- **CPA:** the tax consequences of selling.
- **Insurance professional:** what coverage looks like on a vacant or hazardous property.
- **City or county building, health or fire department:** whether any enforcement notice or local rule applies to the property.

Where to start depends on your situation. If the home was a parent's or relative's, start with the attorney or the title company, because who can sign comes first. If a notice has been posted or a letter has come, start with the city or county. If you are thinking about listing, talk to a listing agent about the disclosure form.

[note] Confirm legal, tax, title, code and insurance points with the right professional for your situation. This guide explains what to ask, not what the answer is for your house.

Once you know who can sign, what is owed and what the city or county says, you can compare keeping it, clearing it, listing it and selling directly with real information.

If a direct sale is one of the routes you want to talk through, the next step is the [packed and hoarded house page](https://www.twinhomebuyer.com/hoarder-houses/).
